name: DocuVision v1.1 Outlook Watch (inbox → intake → task.completed → CSV watch dir)

parameters.content:
## Flow A — Outlook inbox → intake

Sources checked against the repo (as-of 2026-11-15, branch feat/r003-p042-egress):

- Trigger parameters verified in n8n source: event default `messageReceived` (MicrosoftOutlookTrigger.node.ts:122-129); Graph query selects `subject` (MicrosoftOutlookTrigger.node.ts:73); `options.downloadAttachments` puts each attachment into binary fields named `<attachmentsPrefix><index>` = `attachment_0`, `attachment_1`, ... (trigger/MessageDescription.ts:124-136). Credential (Azure AD OAuth) is configured in n8n credentials — never in this file.
- The multipart `inputDataFieldName` resolves the FIRST binary field via expression, so it works with any attachment count.
- `POST /api/v1/upload` — multipart `file` required (backend/tests/snapshots/openapi_baseline.json → Body_upload_file_api_v1_upload_post.required); response keys task_id / file_name / status:"uploaded" / message / page_count from the handler (backend/app/routers/analyzer.py:114-120). Preview-only: its task_id does NOT feed analyze (docstring analyzer.py:88; analyze creates a NEW task_id from its own file, analyzer.py:207-210). Both branches therefore carry the same attachment.
- `POST /api/v1/analyze` — multipart `file` + optional Form fields (analyzer.py:140-174); response model TaskStatus (openapi_baseline → components.schemas.TaskStatus). IMPORTANT: pack.md §2 T5 lists only "附件 POST upload", but upload never triggers processing — the `task.completed` callback only fires from the finalize step of the analyze pipeline (backend/app/orchestration/steps/governance.py:117-128), so this template posts the attachment to BOTH endpoints; analyze is the processing entry.
- `document_type` falls back to `auto` via expression; boolean Form fields accept "1"/"0" only (analyzer.py:181-182), not "true"/"false".
- LOAD DISCIPLINE (R-003/P-042 hardening): this template sends NO `per_order_output_dir` anywhere and never calls the batch API; no absolute path is sent to or read from the backend. See Flow C note and README for the batch-chain trust boundary.

## Flow B — task.completed → CSV to watch dir

- Callback body {event, payload, timestamp} (backend/app/services/webhook_service.py:138); payload task_id / file_name / status / validation_passed per dispatch site governance.py:120-127; status always "completed" (governance.py:85). Only task.completed and batch.completed are dispatched (webhook_service.py:73, 94); failures have NO callback — poll GET /api/v1/tasks/{task_id} (backend/app/routers/tasks.py:31-37).
- GET /api/v1/tasks/{task_id}/result: 400 "Task not completed" unless status in ("succeeded","completed"), 404 unknown task (backend/app/routers/tasks_content.py:30-37). Result body is untyped in the snapshot (200 schema {}); keys assembled in finalize_step governance.py:89-109, including view merged from the envelope (governance.py:95-99).
- view.fields is a DICT: field name → scalar string, or list for items/line_items/findings (assignment backend/app/orchestration/steps/envelope.py:151,153; empty scalars backfilled with "", list keys untouched — backend/app/services/kie/field_merge.py:60+ backfill_schema_keys). The Code node flattens it one row per field; list/object values are JSON-stringified; if view.fields is absent (KIE off) it emits a single `__no_kie_fields__` row so the CSV is still observable — it does NOT invent field values.
- The watch directory is an n8n-side path injected via $env.DOCUVISION_WATCH_DIR (mounted volume). It is a DIFFERENT output from the backend per-order watch dir <OUTPUT_DIR>/per_order/<batch_id>, which the backend writes itself only for batch chains (backend/app/routers/batch.py:138-174).
- Dispatch timeout 15s / 2 retries (webhook_service.py:142,151-161): the Webhook node responds immediately (responseMode onReceived).

## Flow C — one-off registration + batch trust boundary

Registration gates (backend/app/routers/webhooks.py:57-77): backend WEBHOOK_ENABLED=true (default false, alias DOCUVISION_WEBHOOK_ENABLED, config.py:102-105; dispatch no-ops otherwise, webhook_service.py:129-130); header X-DocuVision-Admin-Token must equal WEBHOOK_ADMIN_TOKEN (config.py:106-109; empty token fail-closes 401, webhooks.py:24-46); 200 → {subscription_id, url, events}.

SSRF gate: loopback/private callback URLs are rejected with 400 (webhook_service.py:21-30, 89-90) — $env.DOCUVISION_CALLBACK_URL must be non-loopback from the DocuVision host.

TRUST BOUNDARY for batch chains (R-003/P-042, cited by this template's load discipline):
- `per_order_output_dir` is a caller-supplied option of POST /api/v1/batch `options` JSON (batch.py:207-212). Omit it (or send "") → backend default `<settings.OUTPUT_DIR>/per_order/<batch_id>` (backend/app/services/per_order_export_service.py:44-45; opt-in export only fires when options.per_order=true, batch.py:163).
- Escape attempt → ValueError at batch creation mapped to HTTP 422 (batch.py:185-204, raise at :204; ValueError text per_order_export_service.py:58-66). The service docstring names this exact n8n watch-dir use case (per_order_export_service.py:39-42).
- Therefore: never put a deployment-local absolute path into any request field; let the backend confine it.
